title: The Gates of Paradise
text:
A soldier named Nobushige came to the Zen master Hakuin and asked him, "Is there really a paradise and a hell?"

"Who are you?" asked Hakuin.

"I am a samurai," the warrior replied.

"You, a soldier!" exclaimed Hakuin. "What kind of ruler would have you as his guard? Your face looks like that of a beggar."

Nobushige became so angry that he began to draw his sword. Hakuin went on: "So you have a sword! Your weapon is probably much too dull to cut off my head."

As Nobushige pulled out his blade, Hakuin said, "Here open the gates of hell!"

At these words the samurai understood what the master had done. He put his sword back in its sheath and bowed.

"Here open the gates of paradise," said Hakuin.
lesson: Anger can take you somewhere terrible in a few seconds, and noticing it can bring you back just as fast. Catch the moment before you act.
source: Nyogen Senzaki and Paul Reps, 101 Zen Stories (1919)
caveat: This is a traditional anecdote attached to Hakuin, and similar versions are told of other masters.
